title: Revit governed family content and reusable-content hygiene
test_intent: Determine whether repeatable, scheduled, tagged, or otherwise governed Revit content uses controlled reusable families and governed data carriers rather than uncontrolled duplicates, ad-hoc in-place content, or manual information patching.

applicability.applies_when: The tested Revit model contains loadable families, in-place families, or other governed component content.
applicability.not_applicable_when: No family/component content is present in the tested scope.

required_evidence: applicable family naming and reusable-content rules
parameter and tag/schedule dependencies where relevant
approved library or controlled content source where applicable

result_logic.pass: Applicable reusable content follows governed family identity, source, and information requirements; scheduled/tagged repeatable content is not implemented as uncontrolled in-place content; and any in-place exceptions have sufficient governed rationale/evidence.
result_logic.fail: A positive violation is found, including repeatable or governed content implemented as uncontrolled in-place geometry, duplicate/uncontrolled family identities, manual patching replacing governed information carriers, or an in-place exception without the required rationale/evidence.
result_logic.not_applicable: No family/component content is within scope.
result_logic.indeterminate: The applicable family naming, library/source, parameter, information-need, or exception requirements needed for evaluation are unavailable or incomplete.

provenance.migration_note: Appendix E ATS for family-content hygiene. Exact family catalogues, parameter names, and approval roles remain governed dependencies rather than invented defaults.
